checklist.notes: the utterance clearly marks a finished event; this is a narrow lesson-bound receptive check, not a claim of full objective coverage.
The READY gate, hidden transcript, single question, later transcript release, and tolerant punctuation policy make a clear attempt-feedback cycle.
The protocol reuses a source-lesson utterance and declared scope rather than introducing an unrelated target.
The learner is told to wait for audio, and text-only completion is explicitly disallowed.
One question at a time and bounded output or feedback keep the interaction manageable for the declared tier.
Audio or speech is mandatory and the transcript is initially hidden, so the static protocol is suitable for listening practice.
The short, structured self-study interaction is accessible to Vietnamese learners and avoids unsupported population-wide or accent claims.

findings.description: The opening calls the material an ‘exchange,’ but the private transcript is one speaker utterance and the only question is narrow dictation.
findings.recommendation: Call it an utterance and, in a later expansion, add a meaning-focused question on a separate turn.

limitations: Static protocol wording only was reviewed. No live provider behavior, audio realization, learner response or outcome, provider authentication, human review, or release approval was observed or claimed.
